narration: On the afternoon of January 21st, the house is quiet.

nodes.speaker: Michael Willis
nodes.text: Citizens of this country, thank you for having me. I come with a plain belief that this country is on the edge of something good. This country was never finished. Each generation has been handed it half-built and asked to carry it a little further, and now it is our turn.

nodes.speaker: Michael Willis
nodes.text: I begin this work with a glad heart, because I believe in the people I have come to serve. The oath is a promise to the future as much as to the present, and the future is a thing I am looking forward to.

nodes.speaker: Michael Willis
nodes.text: I believe the next generation will do more with freedom than we dared, and I want to get out of their way. To everyone who voted for someone else: I want your good ideas as much as anyone's, and I will go looking for them.

nodes.speaker: Michael Willis
nodes.text: There is a good deal to be glad about tonight, and I intend to enjoy it with you before we get back to work. Paychecks have grown faster than prices this year, and that is real progress for working people. The economy has grown this year, and the question now is whether that growth reaches the people who do the work. Not everyone has shared in it. Work has grown harder to find, and more Americans are looking for it than a year ago. None of that happened by accident. It happened because millions of people kept showing up, to work and to one another. Every American who wants to work should be able to find it, and until that is true, it is the first thing I will answer for.

nodes.speaker: Michael Willis
nodes.text: To the members of Congress: the people sent us here together, and they will judge us together. I mean to work with you, and I will come to you often.

nodes.speaker: Michael Willis
nodes.text: There is one thing on which I will not move. Federal law answers legal cannabis sales with a no. If a bill on legal cannabis sales reaches my desk, I will not sign it.

nodes.speaker: Michael Willis
nodes.text: I am grateful to Vice President Tamara Guerrero, who will stand beside me in this work and tell me when I am wrong.

nodes.speaker: Michael Willis
nodes.text: This nation is its states before it is any one capital. To the governors and the lawmakers who serve them, I offer a partnership, and an open door.

nodes.speaker: Michael Willis
nodes.text: To the families doing better, I want it to last, and to any who are not, I will not forget you. The road ahead is long, and we will not walk all of it in my time. But we will walk it together, and we begin today. God bless you, and God bless the United States of America.

narration: Late in the morning on March 4th, you've come out to a public place. The crowd goes quiet as you reach the microphone.

nodes.speaker: Michael Willis
nodes.text: Mr. Speaker, and everyone watching, thank you for having me. I come with a plain belief that this country is on the edge of something good.

nodes.speaker: Michael Willis
nodes.text: I come before you glad to report that the country is better placed than it has been in some time, and ready for more.

nodes.speaker: Michael Willis
nodes.text: I believe in the shop on the corner and the family saving to open it, and I think their best years are coming.

nodes.speaker: Michael Willis
nodes.text: There is a good deal to be glad about tonight, and I intend to enjoy it with you before we get back to work. Paychecks have grown faster than prices this year, and that is real progress for working people. The economy has grown this year, and the question now is whether that growth reaches the people who do the work. But work has grown harder to find this year, and there are men and women in every part of the country still looking for it. Hope is not the same as being satisfied. It is the belief that next year can be better than this one, and the willingness to work for it. Every American who wants to work should be able to find it, and until that is true, it is the first thing I will answer for.

nodes.speaker: Michael Willis
nodes.text: There is one thing on which I will not move. On legal cannabis sales, federal law says no. I will not lend my name to legal cannabis sales, and I will say so plainly.

nodes.speaker: Michael Willis
nodes.text: To every parent who lay awake this year wondering how to make it work: I hear you, and I will measure my days by whether your nights get easier. I thank you for your trust, and I will try to deserve it.
